pages.title: CLIENT-SIDE 60FPS WEBM EXPORTER
pages.subtitle: Instant 60FPS Video Export Directly In Browser Memory

pages.title: 01 // THE CLOUD RENDER MONEY PIT
pages.content:
Serverless video rendering on AWS Lambda or GCP Cloud Run sounds great until the bill arrives. Every rendered frame costs CPU time. Every exported video burns bandwidth. Scale to 100,000 exports, and your infrastructure budget collapses.

Why pay cloud servers to render frames when your user's machine has an M3 chip or RTX GPU sitting idle?

pages.title: 02 // IN-MEMORY STREAM SYNTHESIS
pages.content:
We offload video creation 100% to the client browser:
1. Canvas Stream Capture: canvas.captureStream(60) locks output to a deterministic 60 FPS image stream.
2. Web Audio Synthesizer: Procedural Web Audio API generates 120 BPM cyber kicks, sub drops, and high-tech arpeggios in real time.
3. Stream Merging & MediaRecorder: Combines video and audio tracks into VP9/Opus WebM directly in RAM.

pages.title: 03 // THE 0ms QUEUE VICTORY
pages.content:
Click 'Export Video (.webm)' on the bottom Collapsible Dock. The camera executes a 30-second 5-act auto-flight. The browser encodes the VP9 stream live.

When finished, ArtificialCraft_Monolith_60fps.webm downloads instantly.

Server compute cost: $0.00.
Render queue latency: 0ms.
That is how workers build sustainable media pipelines.
